chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'We do not know of any Hajj for Allah other than Al-Mut'ah. When we meet our Lord, we will say: We acted according to Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet. And the people will say: We acted according to our own opinion. So Allah will place us and them wherever He wills.'

key_terms.الْمُتْعَةُ: Al-Mut'ah (a specific type of pilgrimage, often associated with temporary marriage in broader context but here specifically Hajj Mut'ah or the practice of the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Al-Mut'ah in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights 'Al-Mut'ah' (specifically referring to the temporary marriage contract or the specific ritual act depending on scholarly interpretation of the context of Sha'ban) as the known practice of the Imams, contrasting their strict adherence to the Quran and Sunnah against the people's reliance on independent reasoning (ra'y). This distinction underscores a key Shia epistemological principle where the Imams' actions serve as the definitive interpretation of divine law, ensuring their standing on the Day of Judgment is based on revealed truth rather than human conjecture.
